advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] After dispatching autobump.yml, find the dispatched run and wait for it with `gh run watch --exit-status` so a failed bump fails the release job
evidence: .github/workflows/release.yml:377: gh workflow run autobump.yml --repo "$TAP_REPO" --ref main
.github/workflows/release.yml:378: echo "Dispatched ${TAP_REPO} autobump.yml for nava-rebar ${VERSION}"

Nothing after the dispatch finds the resulting run or reads its conclusion. The docs leave that check to a human: `gh run list --repo navapbc/homebrew-rebar --workflow autobump.yml -L1   # expect success`.
advisory.finding: The homebrew_tap job succeeds once `gh workflow run` accepts the dispatch and never checks whether the tap's autobump run finished successfully. If the bump fails (sha fetch, push rejected, formula edit error), the release still goes green and the formula silently stays stale. That is the same invisible-staleness failure this change is meant to fix.
scenarios: The tap's autobump fails on a sha256 or push error after being dispatched; release.yml is green and nobody runs the manual `gh run list` check.
advisory.suggested_fix: After `gh workflow run`, poll `gh run list --repo "$TAP_REPO" --workflow autobump.yml --event workflow_dispatch -L1 --json databaseId,createdAt` until a run created after the dispatch time appears, then run `gh run watch "$id" --repo "$TAP_REPO" --exit-status`.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Decide what homebrew_tap does when the dispatched version will never be PyPI's latest (skip with a notice or fail), and document it
evidence: .github/workflows/release.yml:349-350: curl -fsS https://pypi.org/pypi/nava-rebar/json | python3 -c '...print(json.load(sys.stdin)["info"]["version"])'
.github/workflows/release.yml:357-359: if [ "$served" != "$VERSION" ]; then echo "::error::PyPI did not report nava-rebar ${VERSION} as latest within 5 minutes"; exit 1
The sibling mcp_registry wait checks the per-version endpoint instead (.github/workflows/release.yml:461: "https://pypi.org/pypi/nava-rebar/${version}/json")
docs/releasing.md:603-605 already says a prerelease would need release.yml to skip jobs; homebrew_tap adds another job that would have to be skipped.
advisory.finding: The wait loop requires PyPI's project-level `info.version` (the newest non-prerelease) to equal the dispatched version. Any legitimate release that does not become PyPI's newest version (a patch on an older line, or a PEP 440 prerelease) will poll for 5 minutes and then fail the release run red after the irreversible publish.
scenarios: Releasing 0.15.1 after 0.16.0 is already on PyPI: info.version stays 0.16.0, and the job times out and fails.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Assert the homebrew_tap step waits for PyPI to report `$VERSION` before dispatching. Preferably run the step with a stub `curl` that returns an older version, and check that it exits non-zero without calling `gh workflow run`.
evidence: tests/unit/test_release_workflow_pins.py:443-449 checks only `gh workflow run ...`, `gh workflow enable ...`, and the `disabled_manually)` slice of `run`
No assertion mentions `pypi.org/pypi/nava-rebar/json`, `$VERSION`, `VERSION: ${{ inputs.version }}`, or the `served != "$VERSION"` exit
Diff comment in release.yml: `# The tap bumps to PyPI's reported latest, so wait until that is this version.`
docs/releasing.md (diff): `waits until PyPI reports the dispatched version as latest, then runs gh workflow run autobump.yml`
advisory.finding: The test never asserts the new PyPI wait gate. You could delete the whole curl/seq/sleep loop and its `served != VERSION` failure check and test_homebrew_tap_dispatch_job would still pass. That loop is what keeps autobump from being dispatched before PyPI serves the version. Without it the tap reads the old latest version, does nothing, and the formula falls behind again.
scenarios: A refactor drops the wait loop, or the loop's failure exit is turned into a warning. The dispatch then races the PyPI upload and the tap's autobump is a no-op. The test stays green.
advisory.suggested_fix: Follow the pattern in tests/unit/test_gerrit_verify_triage_comment.py:112-147. Run `bash -c step["run"]` with stub `curl`, `gh` and `sleep` binaries on PATH and VERSION=1.2.3. (a) When curl reports 1.2.2 every time, assert rc != 0 and that the gh stub log has no `workflow run`. (b) When curl reports 1.2.3, assert rc == 0 and that the log contains `workflow run autobump.yml --repo navapbc/homebrew-rebar --ref main`.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Drive the homebrew_tap step through each autobump state (active, disabled_inactivity, disabled_manually, unknown) with a stub `gh`, and assert the exit code and which gh subcommands were called.
evidence: tests/unit/test_release_workflow_pins.py:446: `assert 'gh workflow enable autobump.yml --repo "$TAP_REPO"' in run`
tests/unit/test_release_workflow_pins.py:448-449: `manual = run.split("disabled_manually)", 1)[1].split(";;", 1)[0]` / `assert "exit 1" in manual and "workflow enable" not in manual`
Diff contract in release.yml: `disabled_manually) echo "::error::... was disabled by a person; not re-enabling it"`
advisory.finding: The checks on the state branches are substring checks over the whole script, so they cannot tell whether each `case` branch routes correctly. `gh workflow enable` is only required to appear somewhere in `run`. Moving it before the `case` (so it runs unconditionally), or into the `active)` branch, passes the test. With the enable call placed before the `case`, state=`disabled_manually` re-enables the workflow a person disabled, which is exactly what the diff says must not happen. The test only checks that the `disabled_manually)` text slice does not contain the enable call. The `*)` unexpected-state branch is not covered at all.
scenarios: State is `disabled_manually` and the enable call has been moved above the `case`: the script re-enables the workflow, then exits 1. The test passes.
State is `disabled_inactivity` and the enable call has been moved into `active)`: the dispatch goes to a disabled workflow. The test passes.
advisory.suggested_fix: Parametrize over the state the stub `gh api` returns. For `active`: rc 0, no `workflow enable`, `workflow run` called. For `disabled_inactivity`: rc 0, `workflow enable` called before `workflow run`. For `disabled_manually` and `bogus`: rc != 0, neither `workflow enable` nor `workflow run` called. Before trusting any absence check, assert the gh stub log contains the `actions/workflows/autobump.yml` api call, so the test knows the script actually reached that point.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Replace the classic `repo`-scoped HOMEBREW_TAP_TOKEN with a fine-grained token limited to navapbc/homebrew-rebar (Actions: read/write). Store it as a secret of a protected, main-only environment that the homebrew_tap job declares via `environment:`.
evidence: .github/workflows/release.yml:341: `GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.HOMEBREW_TAP_TOKEN }}`

The homebrew_tap job (.github/workflows/release.yml:326-337) has `needs: publish`, `if: github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'` and `permissions: {}`, but no `environment:`. Compare publish at release.yml:265-267 (`environment: name: pypi`).
docs/releasing.md:36: "Actions secret **`HOMEBREW_TAP_TOKEN`** in `navapbc/rebar` (classic token, `repo` scope;"

The job only calls `gh api repos/${TAP_REPO}/actions/workflows/autobump.yml`, `gh workflow enable` and `gh workflow run` on one repo (release.yml:361-377). A fine-grained token limited to navapbc/homebrew-rebar with Actions: read/write covers all three.

docs/releasing.md:31-34 says the reviewer and main-only policy on the `pypi` environment are "load-bearing" for release authorization. This token sidesteps that boundary because it is not tied to an environment.
dropped.finding: The cross-repo HOMEBREW_TAP_TOKEN is far broader than the job needs, and nothing gates it behind an environment. It is a classic PAT with `repo` scope (write to every repo its owner can reach), held as a repo-level Actions secret. The homebrew_tap job uses it without an `environment:`, so any workflow in navapbc/rebar on any branch can read it. Unlike PyPI publishing, it is not limited by the reviewed `pypi` environment's required reviewers or main-only rule.
scenarios: Someone who can push a branch, or get a workflow run in navapbc/rebar, adds a step that prints or sends out `secrets.HOMEBREW_TAP_TOKEN`. They then hold a classic `repo`-scoped PAT for the token owner and can write to every repo the owner can reach, not just the Homebrew tap.

With that token they can push straight to navapbc/homebrew-rebar's Formula/rebar.rb, pointing brew users at a malicious url/sha256. That skips the PyPI OIDC, attestation and required-reviewer controls the rest of the release path depends on.
dropped.suggested_fix: Create a fine-grained PAT, or better a GitHub App installation token, restricted to navapbc/homebrew-rebar with only Actions read/write permission. Store it as an environment secret, for example on a `homebrew-tap` environment with a main-only deployment-branch policy, or reuse `pypi`. Add `environment: homebrew-tap` to the homebrew_tap job and remove the repo-level secret. Update docs/releasing.md:36-38 and step 3 to describe the narrower token and where it lives.
